narrative.overview: CoWorkSpace is warm professional — indigo accent against clean white surfaces, like a well-designed workspace lobby. It's inviting without being casual, premium without being cold. The interface steps back to let the spaces speak, using generous whitespace, subtle borders, and restrained motion.
keyCharacteristics: Clean white surfaces with warm gray neutrals for depth
Indigo as a confident but restrained accent, never exceeding 10% of any screen
Rounded but not playful — 12px corners on buttons, 16px on cards
Flat surfaces with subtle shadow cues for depth
Motion that conveys state, not decoration

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: The indigo primary accent is used on ≤10% of any given screen. Its rarity is the point.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadows appear only as response to state (hover, focus, modal open).

dos: Do use the indigo accent sparingly — buttons, links, focus rings. Let white space breathe.
Do use rounded-xl (12px) on buttons and inputs, rounded-2xl (16px) on cards.
Do keep shadows subtle and purposeful — flat surfaces at rest, shadows on state change.
Do use Figtree as the sole typeface across both marketing and product surfaces.
Do use Framer Motion for interaction feedback (hover, tap, entrance) and GSAP for scroll-driven choreography.
Do use semantic colors for badges and status indicators (green/confirmed, yellow/pending, red/cancelled).
donts: Don't use the indigo accent decoratively. No gradient text, no heavy borders, no background washes. The One Voice Rule.
Don't use glassmorphism, neon accents, or dark-themed cool startup patterns.
Don't use #000 or #fff without tinting — warm whites and rich near-blacks only.
Don't animate CSS layout properties. Use transform and opacity.
Don't use side-stripe colored borders (border-left/right greater than 1px as accent).
Don't use the hero-metric template (big number, small label, gradient accent).
Don't reach for modals as a first response to state — exhaust inline and progressive alternatives first.
Don't use em dashes in copy. Use commas, colons, or periods.
